implementation_notes: TypeScript's Golden Hammer is the meta-framework: Next.js chosen for an application that serves one HTML page, or a React single-page app chosen for a dashboard with no SEO requirement, or Node chosen for CPU-bound batch work with worker threads added as the patch. The local remedy is the same and is unusually easy to apply here: the decision variables (TTFB, bundle size, hydration cost, edge runtime compatibility) are all measurable in minutes with the framework's own tooling, so a spike against a static or server-rendered alternative is cheap.
idiom_name: one framework/runtime for every workload (Next.js, Node, or a UI library)
pitfalls: A framework adopted for its ecosystem (auth, routing, deployments) rather than for any of its rendering properties.
Server-side rendering for content that is identical for every visitor, adding hydration cost and cache complexity for nothing.
Choosing Node for CPU-bound work and then adding worker threads — the patch for an unexamined decision.
